name_note: GTDB splits the classical genus Campylobacter into several genera, of which Campylobacter_D is one, so the findings cited here are about Campylobacter in the broad sense.

sentences.text: A review describes Campylobacter species as having fastidious growth requirements and environmental sensitivity that have challenged microbiologists since they were recognised as human pathogens in the 1970s.
A systematic review and meta-analysis of Campylobacter bacteraemia included twenty-five retrospective observational studies with 2480 patients and reported a pooled case-fatality risk of 5 percent.

That review describes Campylobacter species as a common cause of acute enteric infections which, in immunocompromised or elderly patients, can lead to extraintestinal infections including bacteraemia.
